description: X5.15. A 0.70 kg robotic peregrine falcon after van der Grinten, Folkertsma, Nijenhuis and Stramigioli (2015): a floating multibond fuselage, two wings of two aeroelastic segments each (compliant joints, strip-theory aerodynamics with C_L and C_D affine in the angle of attack), three tail flaps on first-order servos and a motor-gear-crank flapping drive. A cycle-averaged discrete controller (100 Hz attitude/speed loops, 50 Hz look-ahead path guidance) flies a 220 m x 84 m horizontal 1:2 Lissajous figure of eight with a gentle altitude component at 12 m/s in 60 s. Every number is a measurement of this model on the real worker (design/verify.py).

checks.note: the bird starts on the path at the cruise altitude z0 = 25 m
and at the cruise speed 12 m/s along the start tangent of the figure (its x component U cos(atan(2 B / A)))

periodic flapping: the dominant frequency of the left wing flap angle (the commanded flapping frequency varies slowly between 3.7 and 4.5 Hz over the figure, mean 4.05 Hz; the spectrum peaks where it dwells longest, 3.8 Hz); the tolerance covers that modulation
the motor speed follows the commanded speed N 2 pi f_cmd (rad/s, the reference is N = 28 times the crank speed); the residual is the within-stroke speed ripple of the wing inertia
cross-track error along the Lissajous after convergence (t >= 8 s): measured peak 0.85 m, bound 1.5 m (about 1 % of the 110 m figure and 1.2 wing spans)
